Subject: Demo: quick sync — do you see the wrong TZ in Calendly?

Hi Liam,

Thanks for the interest — excited to show you Redwood. I sent our Calendly link so we could lock in a 11:00 slot next week, but a couple people on my side noticed the event shows up in Pacific Time for us and in BST for your team when they click the link. Could you confirm what timezone your calendar is set to? I want to avoid any DST mixups (we had a case last week where Calendly defaulted to organizer TZ and the customer showed up an hour early).

If Calendly is showing incorrectly for you, two quick workarounds that have worked for customers:
- Pick a time and explicitly set the timezone dropdown in Calendly before confirming (bottom-left).
- If that doesn't work, pick any time and reply with a couple of preferred slots and we'll send a manual invite in UTC.

Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?month=2026-04

I can also share a Chili Piper direct link if you prefer — occasionally that honors the browser locale better.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Hi Camila,

Thanks — our calendar is set to Europe/London (BST). When I open the Calendly link it suggests 11:00, but it shows as 11:00 BST in the booking confirmation and our calendar ends up with 11:00 BST. I think the issue is a mismatch where Calendly is showing slots in your Pacific TZ and then marking them in the customer's TZ after booking, so we're sometimes off by an hour (DST start/stop).

Workaround: if you can send a manual invite with the TZ explicitly set to UTC or include an .ics I can import, that avoids the ambiguity.

Alternatively, Chili Piper worked for us in the past because it forced an explicit TZ on selection. If you have that link, I'd try it.

3) If you prefer Calendly, one quick check on your end: click the timezone dropdown on the booking page and set it explicitly to Europe/London before booking. That should keep the times consistent.

If none of the above works, Marissa or Alex can manually create an invite in UTC and include the explicit TZ in the invite text so it shows correctly for everyone.

Thanks — we want to make this frictionless.
